disclaimer.body_1: Connections allow your assistants to interact with external services (Notion, Slack, GitHub, etc.).
disclaimer.body_2: When an assistant uses a connection, your data is sent to the service via third-party software (MCP server) running on your machine. Apollia does not control this software's code.
disclaimer.body_3: Each connection uses an MCP server maintained by a third-party publisher. Verify the source before installing. Prefer servers from the official catalogue.
disclaimer.body_4: Use of third-party APIs is subject to their terms of service. Apollia cannot guarantee compliance of your usage.
disclaimer.body_5: You can at any time: require approval for each action, view the history of all actions, disconnect a service instantly, delete your stored API keys.

integrations.title: MCP integrations
integrations.message: Connect external tools via MCP servers. Your agents call these tools through the native client — no Python dependencies required.

triggers.title: Trigger types
triggers.message: Cron, interval, file-watch, webhook. Each trigger fires the agent's run() function automatically when its condition is met.

pipelines.title: DAG pipelines
pipelines.message: Wire agents together in directed acyclic graphs. Fan-out, fan-in, conditional branches — all handled by the pipeline engine.

observability.title: Observability
observability.message: Every tool call, memory write, and LLM token is logged in the audit trail. Use it to debug, profile, and audit your agents.

graduation.title: You're ready to build
graduation.message: You know the architecture. Create your first agent with manifest() + run(), install it, and let the runtime handle the rest.

bld.timeout_skip: Take your time — you can replay any step from the progress bar.
bld.step_1: Your workspace. Every agent is a Python module with a manifest() + run() contract.
bld.step_2: Start csv-data-worker. Watch how the runtime loads the module and registers it.
bld.step_3: Every agent exposes manifest() for metadata and run() as the main loop.
bld.step_4: Agents write to memory at their own initiative. Search what they stored.
bld.step_5: Send this message to see how an agent handles a memory-related query.
bld.step_6: Connect external tools via MCP. Your agents call them with no Python dependencies.
bld.step_7: Cron, interval, file-watch, webhook. Each trigger fires run() automatically.
bld.step_8: Wire agents in DAG graphs. Fan-out, fan-in, conditions — pipeline engine.
bld.step_9: Every tool call, memory write, and LLM token is logged in the audit trail.
bld.step_10: You know the architecture. Create your first agent with manifest() + run().

mac_sandbox.title: macOS — tools run without sandbox.
mac_sandbox.body: Linux namespace isolation is not available on macOS. Agent tool calls (bash, file I/O) execute directly in your user session. Only run agents you trust, and review their tool permissions in the manifest.

first_chat.step_1_body: Ask a question in plain language — the agent replies locally, without leaving your machine.

agents.title: Your first assistant is one install away
agents.description: Install a Python agent file or spin one up from a template. Apollia runs it locally, in its own sandbox — no cloud round-trip.

tasks.title: Your task feed is wide open
tasks.description: When an agent runs, its tasks land here — completions, failures, approvals, everything tracked and replayable.

triggers.title: Let your agents run on their own
triggers.description: Triggers launch tasks on a cron schedule, a file change, or a webhook. Declare them in apollia.toml or create one below.

pipelines.title: Chain your agents into workflows
pipelines.description: Pipelines orchestrate multi-agent runs with fan-out, fan-in, and human-in-the-loop steps. Launch one to watch it unfold here.

chat.title: Start a conversation with your agents
chat.description: Ask a question, brainstorm, or hand off a task. Every message stays on your machine — local-first by design.

notifications.title: Silence is golden — until it isn't
notifications.description: Add a desktop or webhook channel so your agents can reach you when they need attention or finish a long run.

integrations.title: Connect your first tool
integrations.description: Apollia speaks MCP — browse the registry or plug in a custom server to extend your agents with file systems, APIs, and more.
